/-!
# Bass–Quillen conjecture

The Bass–Quillen conjecture relates vector bundles (finitely generated projective modules) over
a regular Noetherian ring $A$ and over the polynomial ring $A[t_1, \dots, t_n]$: it predicts that
extension of scalars $M \mapsto M \otimes_A A[t_1, \dots, t_n]$ is a bijection on isomorphism
classes, i.e. that every vector bundle over $A[t_1, \dots, t_n]$ is extended from $A$.

Mathlib does not yet have regular local rings, so this file defines `IsRegularLocalRing`
(a Noetherian local ring whose Krull dimension equals the dimension of its cotangent space) and
`IsRegularRing` (a ring all of whose localizations at prime ideals are regular local rings).

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Bass–Quillen conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bass%E2%80%93Quillen_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Regular local ring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regular_local_ring)
- H. Bass, *Some problems in "classical" algebraic K-theory*, Algebraic K-Theory II,
  Lecture Notes in Math. 342, Springer (1973).
- D. Quillen, *Projective modules over polynomial rings*, Invent. Math. 36 (1976), 167–171.
- T. Y. Lam, *Serre's problem on projective modules*, Springer Monographs in Mathematics (2006).
-/

  isNoetherianRing : IsNoetherianRing R
  ringKrullDim_eq_finrank_cotangentSpace :
    ringKrullDim R = Module.finrank (ResidueField R) (CotangentSpace R)
blocks.docstring:
A local ring `R` is a *regular local ring* if it is Noetherian and its Krull dimension
$\dim R$ equals the dimension $\dim_k \mathfrak{m}/\mathfrak{m}^2$ of its cotangent space over
the residue field $k = R/\mathfrak{m}$ (equivalently, by Nakayama's lemma, the maximal ideal
$\mathfrak{m}$ can be generated by $\dim R$ elements).

The alternative `(maximalIdeal R).spanFinrank = ringKrullDim R` is equivalent by Nakayama; the cotangent-space form was chosen as the canonical one.

class IsRegularRing (A : Type*) [CommRing A] : Prop where
  isRegularLocalRing_localization (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime] :
    IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime p)
blocks.docstring:
A commutative ring `A` is *regular* if its localization $A_{\mathfrak p}$ at every prime ideal
$\mathfrak p$ is a regular local ring. (This does not by itself force `A` to be Noetherian; the
Bass–Quillen conjecture is about regular *Noetherian* rings.)

justification.closest_existing_considered: Nothing in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib; `Algebra.Smooth`/`Algebra.FormallySmooth` were considered but are relative notions (smooth over a base), not absolute regularity.
justification.name: BassQuillenConjecture.IsRegularRing
justification.why_needed: No Mathlib notion of a (Noetherian) regular ring. Defined as: every localization `Localization.AtPrime p` at a prime ideal p is a regular local ring. Noetherianness of A is NOT built in; the theorem takes `[IsNoetherianRing A]` separately so the hypotheses read literally as 'regular Noetherian ring'. Sanity lemma: every field is `IsRegularRing` (so the hypotheses of the conjecture are satisfiable).

@[category API, AMS 13]
theorem isRegularRing_of_field (K : Type*) [Field K] : IsRegularRing K where
  isRegularLocalRing_localization p _ := by
    have h0 : (0 : K) ∉ p.primeCompl := fun h ↦ h p.zero_mem
    have hK : IsField (Localization.AtPrime p) :=
      (RingEquiv.ofBijective _ (Field.localization_map_bijective h0)).symm.toMulEquiv.isField
        (Field.toIsField K)
    exact
      { isNoetherianRing := inferInstance
        ringKrullDim_eq_finrank_cotangentSpace := by
          rw [ringKrullDim_eq_zero_of_isField hK, finrank_cotangentSpace_eq_zero_iff.mpr hK]
          rfl }

@[category research open, AMS 13 14 19]
theorem bass_quillen_conjecture (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] [IsRegularRing A]
    (n : ℕ) :
    (∀ (M N : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module A M] [Module.Finite A M] [Module.Projective A M]
        [AddCommGroup N] [Module A N] [Module.Finite A N] [Module.Projective A N],
      Nonempty (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⊗[A] M ≃ₗ[MvPolynomial (Fin n) A]
        MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⊗[A] N) → Nonempty (M ≃ₗ[A] N)) ∧
    (∀ (P : Type u) [AddCommGroup P] [Module (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) P]
        [Module.Finite (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) P] [Module.Projective (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) P],
      ∃ (M : Type u) (_ : AddCommGroup M) (_ : Module A M),
        Module.Finite A M ∧ Module.Projective A M ∧
          Nonempty (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⊗[A] M ≃ₗ[MvPolynomial (Fin n) A] P)) := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
The **Bass–Quillen conjecture**: let $A$ be a regular Noetherian (commutative) ring and let
$n \geq 0$. Then $M \mapsto M \otimes_A A[t_1, \dots, t_n]$ induces a bijection between the
isomorphism classes of finitely generated projective modules (vector bundles) over $A$ and those
over the polynomial ring $A[t_1, \dots, t_n]$. Concretely:
* (injectivity) if $M$, $N$ are finitely generated projective $A$-modules with
  $M \otimes_A A[t_1, \dots, t_n] \cong N \otimes_A A[t_1, \dots, t_n]$, then $M \cong N$;
* (surjectivity) every finitely generated projective $A[t_1, \dots, t_n]$-module $P$ is
  *extended from $A$*, i.e. $P \cong M \otimes_A A[t_1, \dots, t_n]$ for some finitely generated
  projective $A$-module $M$.

Here $A[t_1, \dots, t_n]$ is `MvPolynomial (Fin n) A` and $M \otimes_A A[t_1, \dots, t_n]$ is
written `MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⊗[A] M`, with its natural $A[t_1, \dots, t_n]$-module structure.

Injectivity is automatic (specialise $t_1 = \dots = t_n = 0$); the content of the conjecture is
the surjectivity statement. Wikipedia states the conjecture rank by rank, as a bijection
$\operatorname{Vect}_r(A) \to \operatorname{Vect}_r(A[t_1, \dots, t_n])$ for every $r$; since
extension of scalars preserves the rank and every idempotent of $A[t_1, \dots, t_n]$ lies in
$A$, this is equivalent to the statement for all finitely generated projective modules.

claims.decomposer_note: Precise form (from the article): for every regular Noetherian commutative ring A, every n and every rank r, M ↦ M ⊗_A A[t_1,…,t_n] is a bijection Vect_r(A) → Vect_r(A[t_1,…,t_n]) on isomorphism classes of finitely generated projective modules; injectivity is automatic (specialize t_i = 0), so the real content is surjectivity — every f.g. projective A[t_1,…,t_n]-module is extended from A — and one may quantify over all f.g. projective modules rather than fixing r (rank need not be constant if Spec A is disconnected); 'regular Noetherian' must be defined bespoke (Noetherian with all localizations at primes regular local rings) since this Mathlib checkout lacks such a predicate; the article's known cases (Quillen–Suslin for fields, Lindel for smooth k-algebras) and the isotropic-reductive-group extension are context, not questions posed by the statement.
claims.reviewer_why: States, for A a regular Noetherian ring ([IsNoetherianRing A] [IsRegularRing A], the latter bespoke: every prime localization is a regular local ring, defined as Noetherian local with ringKrullDim = finrank of the cotangent space) and every n, that M ↦ A[t₁..tₙ] ⊗[A] M is a bijection on isomorphism classes of f.g. projective modules, unpacked as injectivity ∧ surjectivity with Nonempty (≃ₗ). Verified the synthesized A[t]-module instance on the tensor product is TensorProduct.leftModule (rfl + smul law). Quantifying over all f.g. projective modules instead of fixed rank r is permitted by the decomposition notes and is equivalent (idempotents of A[t] lie in A, base change preserves rank). Includes proved API lemmas for the bespoke classes. c03/c04/c08 were equally faithful alternatives; c01/c02/c05/c06 state only the (equivalent) surjectivity form and are also faithful, but c07 is the most literal and best documented. Extra Quillen–Suslin variants in c03/c04/c08 were dropped as context, not the slot.

`IsRegularRing` (a ring all of whose localizations at prime ideals are regular local rings).

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Bass–Quillen conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bass%E2%80%93Quillen_conjecture)

universe u

/-- A local ring `R` is a *regular local ring* if it is Noetherian and its Krull dimension
$\dim R$ equals the dimension $\dim_k \mathfrak{m}/\mathfrak{m}^2$ of its cotangent space over
the residue field $k = R/\mathfrak{m}$ (equivalently, by Nakayama's lemma, the maximal ideal
$\mathfrak{m}$ can be generated by $\dim R$ elements). -/
class IsRegularLocalRing (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] : Prop where
  isNoetherianRing : IsNoetherianRing R
  ringKrullDim_eq_finrank_cotangentSpace :
    ringKrullDim R = Module.finrank (ResidueField R) (CotangentSpace R)

/-- A commutative ring `A` is *regular* if its localization $A_{\mathfrak p}$ at every prime ideal
$\mathfrak p$ is a regular local ring. (This does not by itself force `A` to be Noetherian; the
Bass–Quillen conjecture is about regular *Noetherian* rings.) -/

  isRegularLocalRing_localization (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime] :

/-- Every field is a regular local ring (of dimension $0$). -/

  isNoetherianRing := inferInstance
  ringKrullDim_eq_finrank_cotangentSpace := by
    rw [ringKrullDim_eq_zero_of_field, finrank_cotangentSpace_eq_zero]
    rfl

    rw [IsPrincipalIdealRing.ringKrullDim_eq_one R (IsDiscreteValuationRing.not_isField R),

    rfl

are satisfiable; for fields the conjecture is the Quillen–Suslin theorem. -/

items: The list-page entry is terse; the precise formulation was taken from the Wikipedia article: for a regular Noetherian ring A, M ↦ M ⊗_A A[t_1,…,t_n] is a bijection Vect_r(A) → Vect_r(A[t_1,…,t_n]) on isomorphism classes of f.g. projective modules.

'Bijection on isomorphism classes' is unfolded into an explicit conjunction of injectivity and surjectivity, quantified over modules with `Nonempty (_ ≃ₗ[_] _)` for 'isomorphic', instead of constructing a quotient type of isomorphism classes. The injectivity clause is a known triviality (specialise t_i = 0) but is retained so the Lean statement is literally the bijection asserted by the source.

The rank r is not fixed: the statement quantifies over all f.g. projective modules rather than rank-r ones (as the decomposition notes permit). This is equivalent to the rank-by-rank statement for all r, because base change preserves rank and idempotents of A[t_1,…,t_n] lie in A (so a non-constant-rank case splits into constant-rank cases over the factors of A); it also covers disconnected Spec A.

A[t_1,…,t_n] is `MvPolynomial (Fin n) A`; n ranges over all naturals including n = 0 (trivially true case). M ⊗_A A[t] is written with the algebra on the left, `MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⊗[A] M`, so that Mathlib's `TensorProduct.leftModule` supplies the A[t]-module structure; I checked (with_reducible rfl) that the synthesized instance is exactly `TensorProduct.leftModule` over the standard module structures.
'Vector bundle' is taken to mean finitely generated projective module: `Module.Finite` + `Module.Projective`, as in the article.

Regular local ring is defined as Noetherian local with `ringKrullDim R = finrank_k (𝔪/𝔪²)` (cast ℕ → WithBot ℕ∞; for Noetherian local rings the dimension is finite so this is exactly the standard condition). Regular ring is defined via all prime localizations (the standard definition; quantifying only over maximal ideals would be equivalent by Serre's theorem but is a deeper fact).

Noetherianness of A is a separate hypothesis `[IsNoetherianRing A]` rather than being folded into `IsRegularRing`, mirroring the words 'regular Noetherian ring'. `IsRegularLocalRing` does include Noetherianness (part of the standard definition), which is redundant for localizations of a Noetherian ring but harmless.
All modules live in the same universe `Type u` as A. This is no loss of generality: every f.g. module is isomorphic to a quotient of a finite free module in the universe of the ring.

`set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 100000 in` is placed before the main theorem because Mathlib's `MvPolynomial.module` instance is tried before `Semiring.toModule` and triggers an expensive failing search for `Module (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A) A` when synthesizing `Module A[t] (A[t] ⊗[A] M)`; this only affects elaboration time, not the meaning of the statement.

The two bespoke classes are kept in the problem file (the task allows only one output file); in a real PR they might be moved to FormalConjecturesForMathlib/RingTheory/ as reusable definitions. The API lemmas (fields and DVRs are regular local rings; fields are regular rings) are tagged `category API` and serve as the required basic tests of the definitions, and as evidence the hypotheses of the conjecture are non-vacuous.

Known cases (Quillen–Suslin, Lindel) and the Nisnevich-cohomology/isotropic reductive group extension are mentioned in the article as context only and were not formalized, per the decomposition table.
